# Population-weighted interpolation with tidycensus::interpolate_pw()

# Tracts and wards don't share boundaries. interpolate_pw() splits each
# tract's counts across wards based on where the tract's population lives,
# using 2020 Census block populations as weights. If 30% of a tract's
# population is in Ward 1, Ward 1 gets 30% of that tract's counts.
#
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# Projected coordinate system for DC (NAD83 / Maryland, meters).
# Do spatial calculations in a projected CRS, not latitude/longitude.
```{R}
dc_crs <- 26985
```

# 1. Source data: poverty counts by tract ---------------------------------
# Interpolate counts, not rates. The rate is calculated at the end.
```{R}
poverty <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = c(pov_universe = "B17001_001", pov_below = "B17001_002"),
  state = "DC",
  year = 2024,
  output = "wide",
  geometry = TRUE,
  cb = FALSE # detailed tract boundaries that line up with blocks
) |>
  select(pov_universeE, pov_belowE) |> # keep estimates, drop margins of error
  st_transform(dc_crs)
```

# 2. Weights: 2020 Census blocks with population (POP20) ------------------
```{R}
dc_blocks <- blocks(state = "DC", year = 2020) |>
  st_transform(dc_crs)

``` 
# 3. Target geography: DC wards --------------------------------------------
# Any polygon layer works here, e.g. school attendance zones.

```{R}
wards <- state_legislative_districts(
  state = "DC",
  house = "upper",
  year = 2024
) |>
  select(ward = NAMELSAD) |>
  st_transform(dc_crs)
```

# 4. Interpolate -------------------------------------------------------------
```{R}
ward_poverty <- interpolate_pw(
  from = poverty,
  to = wards,
  to_id = "ward", # use a character ID column
  weights = dc_blocks,
  weight_column = "POP20",
  extensive = TRUE, # TRUE for counts (sums), FALSE for averages
  crs = 26985
)
```

# 5. Calculate the rate from the interpolated counts -----------------------

```{R}
ward_poverty <- ward_poverty |>
  mutate(pov_rate = pov_belowE / pov_universeE)

ward_poverty |>
  st_drop_geometry()
```
# Check: wards cover all of DC, so the totals should match
```{R}
sum(poverty$pov_belowE)
sum(ward_poverty$pov_belowE)

```
# 6. Map -----------------------------------------------------------------------
```{R}
ggplot(ward_poverty) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pov_rate), color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::label_percent()) +
  labs(fill = "Poverty rate") +
  theme_void()
```
